lead: Shopify / SHOP — the pandemic boost runs out
smaller: Digital World Acquisition / DWAC — Truth Social's first screenshot
Cisco Systems / CSCO — the boring beat that pays you back
Gold ETF / GLD — the peace rally meets the doubters
why_lead: The 16 February session delivered the clearest crowd verdict of the week on pandemic-era growth: Shopify -16.04% to 746.85 USD after warning the pandemic boost will fade (CNBC [[n0911]], Al Jazeera [[n2015]]) and Roblox -26.51% to 53.87 USD in its worst post-earnings drop (CNBC [[n0905]], Bloomberg's 'stock-pop narrative' [[n0143]], Boston Globe tying both to the Covid decline [[n1200]]), with Zoom, DocuSign and Peloton weak alongside. It has attention evidence (Forbes, Barron's, Entrepreneur's dip-buy prompt [[n0848]], Bloomberg on the retail rebellion [[n1881]]), a split Smart Money View (BI analysts on competition vs the Shop app case; Druckenmiller's 13F) and observable triggers (746.85 USD, 53.87 USD, DoorDash's 24% after-hours counter-signal [[n0847]], the Fed readout [[n2224]]). Relation to strictly earlier retail notes: 2022-02-16 ran Roblox as a smaller item whose stated break was the after-hours miss; that outcome is now cited only as supporting evidence in a Shopify-led essay, with all-new 16 February citations. Shopify has not been an earlier lead or smaller item; Meta ('metaverse bill', 3–4 and 8 February) appears only through the new Druckenmiller filing story.
why_smaller: Digital World Acquisition / DWAC: the political lottery ticket got its first concrete catalyst, the Truth Social screenshot and launch timing (Forbes [[n1866]], Newsweek [[n1867]], Bloomberg [[n1874]]), with DWAC +4.94% to 85.16 USD. The 2022-02-07 note considered DWAC but had no own-date headline; this is its first appearance.

Cisco Systems / CSCO: a distinct boring-value narrative, the beat-and-raise with $15 bln of buybacks (Reuters [[n1181]]) framed for retail by CNBC's Investing Club [[n1193]]; not covered in earlier notes.

Gold ETF / GLD: the war hedge re-bid as NATO said Russia is increasing troop numbers (CNBC [[n1498]], Guardian [[n1502]], Atlantic Council [[n1606]]) and the Duma request (CBS [[n1503]]); gold +0.82%, GDX +3.20%. Relation to earlier notes: 2022-02-14 ran GDX and the 2022-02-16 lead named the unverified pullback as its invalidation; this is a material update on 16 February evidence, kept secondary.
considered_not_chosen: Upstart / UPST (+35.65% to 148.01 USD, the largest gain on the card): no own-date headline on its results or the cause of the jump beyond Entrepreneur's dip-buy question [[n0848]], so the move is not narrated.
Affirm / AFRM (-42.53% over five sessions): a continuation of the 2022-02-14 item without a new catalyst.
DoorDash / DASH (revenue beat, shares up 24% after hours [[n0847]]): used as the counter-signal inside the lead rather than as a separate pandemic-habit item.
Nvidia / NVDA (upbeat forecast [[n2006]]): Nvidia featured on 9 and 16 February; used only as a contrast in the lead.
Virgin Galactic (-6.61%) and Joby (-8.11%): the 16 February item's give-back without a new catalyst.

Avoided as possibly after cutoff: n1508 (AP 'US official: Russia adds 7K more troops near Ukraine border'), whose briefing may have come after 00:00 UTC on 17 February; the gold item relies on the NATO statements of 16 February instead.
